First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x+1={sec}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}({x}^{2}{sec}^{2}⁡x-{x}^{2}{tan}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{x}^{2}({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}-{0}^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{3}}{64} \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{192}\end{aligned}
$$
